title: The category is used, not constructed from Lefschetz rings
context: Adds realization-side data to CT16/018,049; no new construction from the correspondence rings
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]; MPL_14_087-132 M01 and MPL_14_002-044 M01 [first-pass leads]
body: These pages use an existing category and three comparison functors, without identifying its morphisms with cote 16’s lefschetzien rings. The usual pure-motive construction also specifies correspondences between different varieties, an equivalence relation, composition, tensor products, idempotent completion and Tate twists (Jannsen, 1992, pp. 447–448). The new witness therefore strengthens the realization side of the earlier leads, while leaving the requested historical construction unverified.

title: The elliptic period SL₂ is not the Lefschetz action
context: Differs from CT16/007–018’s raising and lowering operators; adds a test internal to this package
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]; MPL_14_087-132 M04 [first-pass own-idea lead, not reviewed]
body: The \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) displayed in the cancelled elliptic-period draft is different from the Lefschetz action: on \(H^1(E)\) for a smooth elliptic curve, both \(L:H^1\to H^3\) and the lowering map to \(H^{-1}\) vanish. Thus a nontrivial period-group action on that two-dimensional space cannot be this Lefschetz action. Confidence: high, because the degree range of curve cohomology proves the distinction independently of the uncertain superscript on G; this adds to the ledger’s projective-line test without rederiving it.

title: Three kinds of grading and the Tate character
context: Adds a parabolic/Levi construction to CT16/003–004,015–018; differs from a grading of a single operator ring
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]; MPL_14_002-044 B04 and MPL_14_087-132 M04 [first-pass leads]
body: The written j lies in \(B^{\prime}/U^{\prime}\), and a chosen lift has a Levi centralizer; a tensor-compatible grading of the identity on an entire pure Tannakian category instead gives a central cocharacter of its tensor-automorphism group (Deligne & Milne, 1982/2012, Definition 5.1). With the ordinary cohomological convention, the character of a Tate object composed with the weight cocharacter has exponent \(\pm2\), whereas the displayed composite is the identity. The operator-ring grading, the Lefschetz Cartan operator, the Hodge-filtration splitting and the weight cocharacter therefore require separately stated normalizations.

title: Only part of the A–D dictionary is established
quote: conj. de Hodge et de Tate
context: Restates the unresolved part of CT16/044–050 and CN S1; the new excerpt adds no A–D definitions
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]; MPL_14_002-044 §2 and §107 [first-pass summary leads]
body: The operational evidence identifies manuscript A with Lefschetz on algebraic classes and manuscript C with algebraicity of inverse Lefschetz operators, corresponding to printed A and B respectively (Grothendieck, 1969a, pp. 195–197). The implications A plus index ⇒ B and D ⇒ rational characteristic-polynomial coefficients make manuscript B = printed D and manuscript D = printed C plausible, but do not supply standalone definitions of the manuscript letters. Those last two correspondences remain provisional, and no new secure definition appears in these 49 scans.

title: The singular-hypersurface programme needs the missing cote 14 witness
context: Differs from CT16/047’s proposed reduction; no implementation in new15/18 and no full cote14 source supplied
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]; MPL_14_002-044 §2 and MPL_14_087-132 M01 [first-pass, truncated leads]
body: CT16/047 withdraws a reduction through smooth hypersurfaces because of the simply-connected obstruction and proposes reformulating standard conjectures for singular varieties. The smooth-projective construction sought on new scan 223 serves the different problem of comparing archimedean cohomology rings. With the actual cote 14 pages absent, this package neither confirms nor refutes that cote 14 carries out the singular-hypersurface programme.

title: The local extension and the arithmetic motivic exact sequence
quote: ext. de E de π par G′(C)
context: Adds a local splitting comparison; differs from the extension by Γ_Q requested in context/README.md, planning section; CT54/003,007 concerns other extensions
body: The displayed sequence has kernel \(G^{\prime}(C)\) and quotient π, so it is not a written witness of \(1\to G_{\mathrm{mot}}(\overline{\mathbf Q})\to G_{\mathrm{mot}}(\mathbf Q)\to\underline{\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q)}\to1\). For compatible rational Nori fibre functors the latter is a modern theorem of Galois descent, exact as affine group schemes, with the last term proconstant over \(\mathbf Q\) (Kahn, 2025, Theorem 5.10 and §10). The real-component discussion on 15/215 does not provide a proof of that arithmetic sequence, a canonical splitting, or an identification of its kernel with the identity component.

title: Nori/Ayoub comparison and algebraic correspondences
context: Adds explicit groups and comparison torsors to CT16/048–049 and CN S15’s programme
ledger: MPL_14_087-132 M23 and MPL_14_002-044 M28a [first-pass leads]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]; S15 named in README, not a separate ledger row
body: Over a subfield of \(\mathbf C\) with a fixed embedding, Choudhury and Gallauer Alves de Souza (2017, Theorem 9.1) identify Nori’s and Ayoub’s classical motivic Galois groups; their theorem allows principal-ideal-domain coefficients, in particular \(\mathbf Q\). The rational pure Nori category is semisimple and agrees with André’s motivated category, as anticipated in the supplied leads (Arapura, 2013, Theorems 6.3.3 and 6.4.1). Identifying every inverse Lefschetz morphism or projector in those categories with an algebraic cycle is a further comparison requiring the relevant standard conjecture, not a consequence of the group construction.

title: Fullness of Hodge realization remains a separate assertion
context: Adds realization fullness to CT16/044,049; differs from pure semisimplicity in CN S15
ledger: MPL_14_087-132 M23 and MPL_14_002-044 M28a [first-pass leads]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]
body: The manuscript expressly invokes conjectural Hodge and Tate input, which is not removed merely by constructing Nori’s category. Arapura (2013, §7.1) separately formulates Nori’s Hodge full-faithfulness conjecture and proves an abelian-type case. Its general essential image is an additional problem, as the manuscript’s double question mark already records.

title: Integral finiteness and positive characteristic need separate arguments
context: Adds integral fibre functors and crystalline points to CT16/014–018 and CT54/005–007; no integral finiteness proof there
ledger: WG2 §2.3 #3 and WG2 S28 (§1.7) [unchecked plans]; MPL_7_061-072+8_001-078 Scan 061 (§66) [first-pass lead]
body: The modern group comparison even has a principal-ideal-domain version, but this does not prove finiteness of the manuscript’s integral fibre-functor forms or classification of positive-characteristic crystalline points. Those require a specified integral category, representability and arithmetic finiteness arguments, and a realization theory with its F,V and filtration data. The supplied integral Lefschetz warnings and p-primary extension notes are checks on these extra requirements, not proofs that the requirements hold.
